Рекомендации Стивена Кови универсальны, поскольку основаны на том, что он называет «естественными законами», – на принципах и правилах, действующих везде и всегда. 
«Семь навыков» могут одинаково успешно использоваться в любой сфере жизни и бизнеса, в любой стране и в условиях любой национальной культуры.

Успехов!

Name: ЭКСТРАСЕНС
Description:
Как развить свои «парапсихические» способности.
Методика Джорджа Крескина.
Джорджа Крескина называют «Нострадамусом XX века».
Наблюдательность, сила внушения, гипноз, знание человеческой натуры, телепатия, выявление лжи, экстрасенсорная чувствительность – все эти и многие другие «сверхспособности» не являются уделом «магов» и «экстрасенсов», но при соответствующей подготовке доступны каждому человеку и опираются исключительно на мощь и гибкость нашего сознания и тела.
Крескин прославился тем, что всю свою жизнь посвятил изучению возможностей человеческого сознания, он выиграл в ТВ шоу «The World’s Youngest Hypnotist» (аналог нашей «Битвы экстрасенсов»)
Крескин про себя всегда говорит: «Я не маг и не экстрасенс. В том, что я делаю, нет совершенно ничего сверхъестественного.  Я изучаю возможности человеческого сознания, присущие каждому из нас с рождения». 

Здоровья и благополучия!

Name: Язык тела
Description:
Метод Аллана Пиза позволит «читать любого человека как книгу», выбирать правильную линию поведения, чувствовать себя уверенно и непринужденно в любой обстановке, принимать самые верные решения – все это теперь реально и доступно каждому.

Знание языка тела (значение различных жестов, мимики и т.д) - на Западе обязательно для менеджеров, начиная со среднего звена.

Мимика, жесты и телодвижения способны выдать истинные мысли. Ведь, как правило, мы на уровне интуиции распознаем неосознанные движения собеседника, формируя определенное отношение к нему. Иногда совершенно непонятно, почему человек неприятен, если он ничего плохого не сделал вам. А причиной антипатии и могут послужить полученные сигналы на уровне языка тела.

Изучайте я  ык телодвижений, и вы непременно добьетесь успеха во всем!

Удачи и процветания!

Name: Хиромантия
Description:
В приложении вы погрузитесь в мир одной из самых таинственных и увлекательных наук - хиромантии.

- научитесь предсказывать судьбу
- узнаете много интересного о характере окружающих вас людей
- по знакам и символам на руке определите, насколько здоров тот, кому вы гадаете.

Будьте здоровы и счастливы!

Name: АнтиСтресс
Description:
Как бороться со стрессом.

Умение управлять стрессом дает огромные преимущества:

• Вы почувствуете себя полным энергии и энтузиазма.
• Вы будете мыслить ясно и логично.
• Ваше самочувствие улучшится, вы будете прекрасно выглядеть.
• Повысится работоспособность, появится творческий подход к работе.
• Вам будет намного легче сохранять спокойствие.
• Вы будете быстрее восстанавливать утраченные силы.
• Вы будете знать, что есть надежное средство немедленно ослабить стресс.
Знать, что это вы контролируете стресс, а не наоборот, – большое облегчение.

Курс Кейта Кинана, дипломированного психолога со степенью бакалавра, магистра философии.

Желаем счастья и благополучия!

Name: Тайны чисел
Description:
Люди гораздо больше зависят от чисел, чем это принято осознавать.

В приложении:
 - Основы нумерологии,
- Нумерологичские расчеты,
- Число жизненного пути и расшифровка,
- Число дня рождения и расшифровка,
- Число экспрессии и расшифровка,
- Число душевного побуждения и расшифровка,
- Число личности и расшифровка
и т.д.,
-Нумерология и здоровье.
Наука нумерология, ее прогнозы и предсказания индивидуальны для каждого. 
Нумерология как система знаний об окружающем нас мире отвечает на любой вопрос, который может у вас возникнуть. 

Приложение познакомит вас с удивительным миром чисел, которые окружают нас от самого рождения до конца жизненного пути.

Удачи и процветания!

Name: Лучшие ГАДАНИЯ
Description:
В приложение – лучшие гадания! 

- гадания на картах
- гадания на костях
- гадание на кофейной гуще
- на чайных листьях
- гадание по морщинам, родинкам
- гадание по цвету глаз
- гадания на самоцветах
- книжное гадание
- гадание на растениях, цветах

и другие самые известные гадания со всего мира.
    
Гадать можно фактически с помощью любого предмета, и заняться этим может каждый человек – и пусть это порой превращается в светскую забаву, но на самом деле гадание – опасный инструмент, обращаться с которым следует бережно, ведь оно в один момент способно изменить нашу грядущую жизнь.
И помните – узнать будущее, можно лишь познав самого себя. И это – главный секрет любого гадания, ведь все ответы скрыты внутри нас, надо лишь правильно задавать вопросы.

Желаем удачи!

Name: Стихи ДЕТЯМ
Description:
Детские стихи Агнии Барто
РЕКОМЕНДОВАННО К ПРОЧТЕНИЮ ДЕТЯМ !
Самые любимые стихи нашего детства.
В приложении несколько сотен стихов – добрых, веселых, умных, красивых!
С картинками!

Уронили мишку на пол,
Оторвали мишке лапу.
Всё равно его не брошу —
Потому что он хороший.

Я люблю свою лошадку,
Причешу ей шёрстку гладко,
Гребешком приглажу хвостик
И верхом поеду в гости.

Почему сегодня Петя
Просыпался десять раз?
Потому что он сегодня
Поступает в первый класс.
.......

Мне теперь не до игрушек —
Я учусь по букварю,
Соберу свои игрушки
И Серёже подарю.
.......
Стихи Барто веселы и интересны даже крохам! 

Растите счастливыми и умными!

Name: Новорожденный
Description:
Приложение – ДЛЯ РОДИТЕЛЕЙ – для тех, кто родителями уже стали, и особенно для тех, кто собирается стать ими.

В этом приложении мы постарались помочь маме и папе усвоить главные принципы ухода и воспитания. Но реализовывать их на практике вам придется самим – тут уж помощи ждать не от кого.
И создано это приложение для людей обыкновенных, живущих обыкновенной человеческой жизнью.
Рекомендации практикующего врача Комаровского Е.О. – заведующего отделением детской областной больницы.

Приложение содержит не только математические головоломки: наряду с арифметическими и геометрическими, представлены головоломки из области физики, мироведения и логики.

Наш ум можно сравнить с нашим телом, если не тренировать тело мускулы быстро утратят гибкость и ослабеют. И точно также, в случае, если мы не будет тренировать мозг работать, мускулы разума станут медлительными и ленивыми.

Приглашаемвас в увлекательный мир головоломок, в мир где вы сможете совершенствовать свой разум и развить свой интеллект.
Получайте удовольствие!

Name: Interference
Description:
Discover Interference - the hit drawing game - and get ready to draw, describe and laugh. You've heard of Chinese Whispers and Broken Telephone, this is our new take on old favourites where you can get creative and laugh your socks off!

Join a chain of players and take turns to draw and describe - but each player can only see the previous step in the game. It won't take long for the original message to get lost in translation and turn into something completely different. You'll love the suspense of waiting to find out what the next person thought your drawing was – it's hilarious to see the whole game when it's finished!

Don't know what to draw? That's fine – join a game and you'll get a description to illustrate in any way you like. You have 10 minutes to draw it before it is given to the next player to describe! Feeling a bit shy about drawing? You can choose to just describe if you like – and move the game on by being as detailed as you can! It is amazing how the first description and the last differ so much! 

You don't need to be a great artist to enjoy this fun and free drawing game - we love stick figures and anything that gets the message across! We have a friendly community packed full of players from all ability levels working together to pass the message on. All you need is your sense of humour!


Features:

* Draw using stylus or touch
* Collect in-game achievements
* Improve your drawing skills & learn from other players
* Compete for 'Picture of the Week'
* Receive likes from other players and be featured on the front page!
* Watch replays of drawings
* Make new friends through art & chat in our welcoming forum

...and most important: Enjoy getting creative and reconnect with your inner artist!


Follow us on social media for updates, features, competitions and much more!

- Facebook: facebook.com/playinterference
- Twitter: twitter.com/playifx
- YouTube: youtube.com/playinterference

Dots, also known as Dots-and-Dashes, Dots and Boxes, Square-it, or the Dots Game, is a classic pen and paper game where two opponents take turns connecting dots through lines to form 4-sided boxes. Each player who completes the fourth side of a 1x1 box earns one point and takes another turn. The opponent with more boxes at the end of the game wins.

Each match takes few minutes, making this game ideal to play when you have short breaks of free time.

This version of Dots is great for beginners, with simple animations and tutorials, but also has a very strong AI, that will challenge the most advanced players.

Checkers, also known as Draughts, is a board game where two players compete to immobilize or ‘eat’ all the opponent pieces. The board pieces can move forward or jump to eat an opponent piece. If a piece reaches the opposite end of the board, it becomes a “king” and can move in any direction.

Checkers Pro has the strongest AI in Windows and Windows Phone – it *will* challenge advanced players. It also offers a fun experience for beginners, with lower difficulty levels and showing possible moves.

RULES of ENGLISH CHECKERS:
* If a piece can jump, it must jump (can be turned off)
* Black always starts
* 8 x 8 board
* No flying kings

FEATURES:
* Play with anyone worldwide!
* Online chat
* Worldwide online high scores
* True-high-res graphic themes
* One-touch move, and drag & drop piece
* 7 difficulty levels: novice to impossible
* New super hard Level 8, “Grok”
* 1 or 2 player mode
* Turn On/Off forced jumps
* Beginner levels 
* Auto-save: don’t lose games if you get a phone call
* Undo: back up wrong moves, try out different strategies
* Always fun: the phone plays differently every time
* Many options: sound, numbering, one-touch move

Name: Backgammon Pro
Description:
The #1 most downloaded Backgammon app, THANK YOU!

Backgammon is a board game where two players compete to get all their 15 pieces off the board before the opponent. Board pieces move based on dice throws.

This is a game of skill. A single game can be decided by luck, but the more one plays, the more the skill is important. After ~30 games the true skill emerges. Even a beginner can beat an expert through luck of draw in a single game, but after several games the skill prevails.

This version of Backgammon uses an advanced neural network in the highest levels, and will challenge advanced players. It also offers a fun experience for beginners, with lower difficulty levels and showing possible moves.

The scoring is based on the official Backgammon ELO system, with each game increasing or reducing rating points every game or match.

FEATURES:
=========
* Worldwide online high scores
* Play a Trial Game, or a Scored Game that counts towards your score
* High res graphic board
* Dice statistics history
* Real time probability calculation
* Achievements
* Tutorials
* 4 difficulty levels: easy to hard
* 1 or 2 player mode
* Many options:
    - Money or Match play style
    - Doubling cube
    - Sound on/off
    - Show possible moves
    - Animation speed
    - Auto-throw-dice
    - Strict tournament rules
    - Dice randomness 
    - Show PIP and point numbers
    - Try different moves, then ‘accept’ or ‘undo’
    - Beaver rule
* Auto-save: don’t lose games in progress
* Always fun: the phone plays differently every time

Available for Windows 10 and Windows 8.

VERSION HISTORY
===============
v2.1 - Enhanced for Windows 10, better resizing, high scores working
v1.99 - Ad option to remove ads for free, UI improvements, keyboard shortcuts (ESC=back, U=Undo), save to roaming storage to preserve all settings and statistics even when reinstalling
v1.15 - optimized for WP8, fast app resume, larger screens, higher resolution icon
v1.14- faster dice rotation when there is a cube
v1.13- new Mercenne Twister random algorithm, faster dice rotation when possible, do not throw dice if bar is full
v2.11-2.12 - bug fixes, UI fixes, optimizations for Windows 10

Name: Helium Streamer
Description:
Helium Streamer for Windows 8.1 is the ultimate way to stream your music from your PC to any Windows 8.1/Windows RT device.

Helium Streamer allows you to search your music collection, browse your favourite artists, albums and tracks as well as genres, years, playlists and more.

The app requires an installation of the free Helium Music Manager software on your PC.
Helium Music Manager can be downloaded from: http://www.helium-music-manager.com

When a track is played, the now playing view allows you full control over the position and shows details about the current artist and track such as lyrics, biography, discography and appearances.

Full support for "Play To" devices meaning that you can change the output source to a TV, Stereo or a similar device with just one click.

Features
+ Easily stream and play music from your Helium Music Manager music collection
+ Search Helium Music Manager's library for albums, artists, titles, genre, years
+ Browse contents of playlists and smart playlists as well as play them 
+ Browse Favourite Album, Artist and Tracks and play or enqueue them
+ Full support for Helium Music Manager's multi-user capability (Network Edition only), allowing per-user ratings, playlists and favourites
+ Last.fm scrobbling support
+ Full "Play To" device support allowing you to play your music to any "Play To" enabled device such as a TV, stereo or similar device
+ Full support for background audio (allows you to listen to your music whilst working in other apps) as well as the built-in miniplayer
+ Lyrics shown for the playing track
+ Full support for tablet hardware keys, allowing easy control of volume
+ Special views to explore in detail artist information such as artist picture, statistics, biography, discography and appearances
+ In detail album information with picture and track lists
+ Per-CD grouped album views
+ Set rating and favourite status for the currently playing track
+ Full subtrack support
+ Built in play queue handling 
+ Translations: English, Swedish and German

Requirements
+ Helium Music Manager version 9.5 or greater - Free, Premium and Network editions all works. The most recent version is recommended.
+ Wi-Fi/Network connection to the PC running Helium Music Manager. 3G also works but requires a little more configuration.

Getting started:

Helium Music Manager - Options (on Windows PC)
1. Open Options from the Tools > Options menu
2. Scroll to the bottom in the left list and select Remote control (available under the Advanced header)
3. Setup the Port to use (default is 8080)
4. Checkmark "Enable remote controlling using Helium Remote"
5. Click OK.

Helium Streamer settings on Windows 8.1
When you start the Helium Streamer app for the first time you will be asked for:

+ The Address of the Windows PC running Helium Music Manager 9.0+ (e.g. 192.168.0.2)
+ The Port number (as defined in Helium Music Manager - Options, see above).

Name: Helium Remote
Description:
Helium Remote is a client application that enables you to remotely control Helium Music Manager. 

An installation of Helium Music Manager is required on your PC to be able to use this application.

Helium Music Manager can be downloaded from www.helium-music-manager.com.



This application is ideal if you want to control Helium Music Manager away from your PC. 
It uses the Wi-Fi connection to receive playing information and to send control commands to Helium Music Manager from anywhere in and around your home. 
You can therefore become a remote DJ and control music for your parties without having to be near to your PC. 



Features
+Easily control Helium Music Manager from your sofa
+Play or Pause your music
+Select Next or Previous track
+Full control of music volume
+Full control over tracks in the Play queue
+Album artwork and details shown for playing track
+Browse Playlists/Smart Playlists and play or enqueue them 
+Browse Favourite Album, Artist and Tracks and play or enqueue them 
+Explore artist/groups in a visually attractive way
+Search Helium Music Manager's library for albums, artists, titles, genre, years and publishers - play or enqueue found tracks
+No additional software to Helium Music Manager required on PC
+Support for English, German and Swedish languages

Requirements
+This application requires Helium Music Manager version 9.5 or greater. (works well with the free version). The most recent version is recommended.
+Wi-Fi or 3G/4G connection to the PC running Helium Music Manager

Name: 0h h1!
Description:
0h h1 is a little logic game.
It follows three simple rules:

    Three red tiles or three blue tiles next to each other in a row or column isn't allowed
    A full row or column must have as many blue tiles as it has red ones
    No two rows are the same. No two columns either.

Simply tap a tile to make it red or blue and complete the grid.
0h h1 gives you unlimited puzzles for all four grid sizes: 

4 x 4
6 x 6
8 x 8
10 x 10

0h h1 is a little gift to you. We hope you enjoy it.

Name: AC Biology: The Effect of Temperature on Enzyme Activity
Description:
Go beyond the standard textbooks and take learning to the next level. Complete virtual experiments, consider exploratory scenarios, make predictions and conclusions—learn science in a whole new way.

In a virtual laboratory setup, you’ll experiment with potato extracts and the enzyme amylase to observe the effect that temperature has on enzyme activity. Then learn about the benefits of a fever in fighting infection but also the dangers of high body temperatures.

•	Discover how temperature affects enzyme activity.
•	Conduct an experiment on the effect of temperature on enzymes.
•	Gather data to test your hypothesis.
•	Identify the optimal temperature range for enzyme activity using a graph.
•	Learn how a fever due to infection can denature enzymes.

Name: AC Biology: Classification of Animals
Description:
Learning science is most effective when it’s engaging as well as educational. Take part in hands-on activities as you discover how to classify animals.

With so many organisms on Earth, it’s no surprise that classifying them according to their characteristics is highly important and useful. Using X-ray and magnifying tools, you’ll first examine the internal and external features of animals. Then you must learn to use a dichotomous key to classify each animal.

•	Learn about eight different types of animals.
•	Examine an animal’s characteristics, such as its vertebrae, skin, or limbs.
•	Classify animals using a dichotomous key.
•	Understand the structure of dichotomous keys.

Name: AC Life Science: DNA Structure
Description:
There’s a new way to learn science! Test your skills and discover new concepts with highly interactive activities that take learning to a different level.

Assist a DNA lab in repairing the damaged DNA structure of an endangered black-footed ferret. In doing so, you’ll learn about the structure of DNA and the relationships between nucleotides and how they form our DNA. 

•	Study the structure of DNA.
•	Correctly pair the four nucleotide bases (guanine, cytosine, adenine, and thymine).
•	Explore the role of DNA in the nucleus of cells.

Name: AC Biology: Factors Influencing Photosynthesis: Temperature
Description:
Become an active participant in your learning with engaging and interactive learning opportunities.  Complete experiments, answer questions, make predictions, and take quizzes—learn science in a new way.

Determine how temperature affects photosynthesis. Learn the chemical equation for photosynthesis, discuss whether temperature affects it, conduct experiments, and explore the role of enzymes in photosynthesis.

•	Define photosynthesis as it relates to plants converting light energy into usable chemical energy.
•	Analyze a graph to determine the optimum temperature in which photosynthesis occurs.
•	Identify the substances required and the products of photosynthesis.
•	Discuss the impact of temperature differences on the rate of photosynthesis.
•	Design and conduct a scientific experiment focused on photosynthesis.

Name: AC Biology: Domains and Kingdoms
Description:
Learn science with real-life scenarios, virtual experiments, exploratory activities, and animations that bring the subject matter to life. Go far beyond the standard textbook and see where it takes you.

In Domains and Kingdoms, a team of scientists has discovered some mysterious frozen cells near a meteor crater and need your help identifying them. Using an interactive laboratory, perform various tests on the mysterious cell samples to determine if they can be classified into one of the six known kingdoms of life.

•	Learn about the six kingdoms into which all life can be classified.
•	Review the modern classification system.
•	Conduct experiments on cell samples in order to identify them.
•	Look closely at the organisms’ cell structure under an interactive microscope.
•	Perform an iodine test to determine how the cells store carbohydrates.

Name: AC Life Science: Mutualism
Description:
Study the relationships that exist among different species in nature with interactive learning opportunities. Complete experiments, answer questions, make predictions, and take quizzes—learn science in a whole new way.

Play the role of an Egyptian plover bird and step inside the mouth of a crocodile! Then observe how two different species are affected when they are together or separate. In doing so, you’ll learn more about mutualism and study examples of other types of symbiotic relationships.

•	Find out why a plover bird might risk its life by standing in the mouth of a crocodile.
•	Make predictions about how the crocodile and bird will interact.
•	Observe how two different species are affected when they are together or separate.
•	Analyze graphs of data showing changes among the species, and then make conclusions.
•	See if you can correctly identify organisms that have mutualistic relationships.

Name: AC Biology: Natural Selection
Description:
There’s a better way to learn and experience the world of science. Take part in interactive, highly visual activities that let you manipulate objects in a virtual environment to learn all about them.

Consider one of the key components of Charles Darwin’s theory of evolution: natural selection. Using an example of blue jays feeding on moths, observe how natural selection affects the blue jay population as their environment changes.

•	Learn the meaning of natural selection.
•	Discover how environmental changes affect a species’ survival.
•	Predict which moths the blue jays will eat.
•	Learn how genetically controlled traits can change over time.

Name: AC Biology: Investigating Photosynthesis with Van Helmont
Description:
Discover a new way to learn with engaging explorations, experiments, and animations in an interactive environment. Learn by doing and see the impact of being involved in what you learn.

Repeat van Helmont’s experiment, as well as a modern follow-up experiment, to show where plants obtain their mass. After learning that plants do not gain mass from soil or water, and conducting experiments that involve weighing plants as they grow, you can establish that plants gain mass from air. Review photosynthesis and all that you learn from the experiments.

•	Establish what van Helmont’s experiment was about.
•	Explain how plants get their mass.
•	Understand the importance of careful measurement when doing scientific investigations.
•	Analyze data and develop a conclusion.
•	Use math in scientific inquiry.

Name: AC Life Science: Human Body Systems
Description:
Get involved in learning with highly interactive and engaging science activities. It’s all about doing and becoming an active participant in your own learning. The time is now, so get started and see where it takes you.

Robo Bio 09, a robot capable of simulating the human body, has reports of errors in some of its systems. It is up to you to conduct quality control tests in order to identify and resolve these errors. By doing so, you’ll learn about the different systems in the human body and their functions.

•	Investigate the digestive, circulatory, respiratory, excretory, skeletal, and muscular systems of the human body.
•	Perform a transplant on the robot to fix an issue, if necessary.
•	Feed the robot to increase its energy level.
•	Make adjustments to the robot’s oxygen or waste levels.
•	Learn about the division of labor in the human body.
•	Study how the different systems in the body interact and work together.

Name: AC Biology: Energy Flow From Producers to Consumers
Description:
Go beyond the standard textbooks and take learning to the next level. Take part in virtual investigations, use simulations and models, collect data and analyze graphs—and do it all right there on your device!

Using a national park simulator, you must find the right balance of biotic and abiotic factors in order to create an ecosystem model that is stable over time. In doing so, you’ll learn how energy flows through the components of an ecosystem.

•	Differentiate between biotic and abiotic factors.
•	Explore the effects of abiotic factors on plant and animal populations.
•	Interpret a biomass pyramid.
•	Understand the hierarchy of energy flow between producers, primary consumers, and secondary consumers.
•	Create a sustainable ecosystem.

Name: AC Life Science: Dancing with the Bees: Animal Communication
Description:
Be actively involved in how you learn. Interactive explorations and informative animations help you to learn science by doing it, not just reading about it. So jump in and see where it takes you.

Discover how bees communicate information about food sources to members of the hive. Then test your skills at interpreting various bee dances in order to correctly identify the locations of different nectar sources.

•	See how bees use dances as a form of communication.
•	Interpret bee dances to correctly locate nectar sources.
•	Discover the differences between the bees’ round and waggle dances.
•	Find out how bee dances are an example of a behavioral adaptation.

Name: Biology: Introduction to Photosynthesis
Description:
Personalized… Interactive… Engaging… Instructional

A New Way of Learning Starting Today! The AC VBook!

Enter the ever-growing AC VBook library and get started with Biology ― Introduction to Photosynthesis.  Jump into the world of a standards-based textbook with a difference: highly interactive explorations, visual explanations and exercises—all focused on understanding important biology concepts.

It’s biology like you’ve never seen before.  

Learn about it. See it in action. Practice it. Check your understanding. And do it all on your Windows 8 tablet or computer.


Investigate the different scientific experiments leading to the discovery of photosynthesis.

Discover just what makes plants grow.

Examine the different factors critical to photosynthesis.

Explore the impact of chemicals on photosynthesis.

Discover how a steelyard balance works.

Understand the results of a starch test and how it can be used to investigate plants.


The AC VBook Biology – Introduction to Photosynthesis walks you through the following topics:

Early Experiments on Photosynthesis
	Studies of Jean Baptista Van Helmont
	Do Plants Grow by Drawing Material from the Soil?
	What Was the Missing Factor That Van Helmont Did Not Consider?
	Let’s Investigate More to Find the Source of the Additional Mass
	Van Helmont’s Studies and Beyond
	Do Plants Grow by Getting Material from the Air?
	Does Light Have Any Effect on the Experiment?

Where Do Plants Get Their Mass as They Grow?
	Wrap It Up
	Work on My Own

Discovering the Equation for Photosynthesis
	What Do Plants Produce?
	How Do We Conduct a Starch Test?
	What Factors Do Plants Need to Conduct Photosynthesis?
	The Chemical Formula for Photosynthesis
	What Is Photosynthesis?
	Wrap It Up
	Work on My Own

Summary
	Early Experiments on Photosynthesis
	Discovering the Chemical Equation for Photosynthesis

Name: AC Life Science: Habitat Designer: Sea Turtles
Description:
Learn science in a way that is engaging and effective. Complete interactive actvities and quizzes, access helpful feedback and key vocabulary―and do it all right there on your device!

Loggerhead sea turtles are endangered but you can help by designing a habitat that best protects them. To be successful, you must consider the most appropriate elements that will help the sea turtles survive.

•	Examine the components of ecosystems and populations.
•	Access information about the habitat requirements of sea turtles.
•	Choose the appropriate size for the turtles’ habitat.
•	Learn about different types of ecosystems.
•	Select the best flora and fauna for the turtles’ habitat.
•	Choose the most suitable monitoring systems and fencing structures to protect the turtles.

Name: AC Life Science: Plants' Needs for Photosynthesis
Description:
The time has come to experience science like never before! With engaging and highly interactive activities, you… See it... Do it... Practice it... Apply it. Bring science to your device and take control of your learning.

Determine what plants require to perform photosynthesis. Using four variables (water, carbon dioxide, oxygen, and sunlight), conduct a starch test and discover the factors necessary for photosynthesis. Learn that glucose (sugar) and oxygen are products of photosynthesis, and that plants store glucose as starch.

•	Make a hypothesis or prediction before the experiment.
•	Investigate the products of photosynthesis.
•	Interpret data to come to a conclusion about photosynthesis.
•	Discover what is needed for photosynthesis to occur.
•	Understand where photosynthesis occurs within a plant.

Name: AC Physics: Combining Parallel and Perpendicular Forces
Description:
There’s a new, engaging way to learn and apply your knowledge of science in a dynamic environment. Learn by doing and see the impact of being involved in what you learn.

Test your skills at determining the magnitude and direction of the net force when two parallel or perpendicular forces act on an object such as a truck or a ship. Plot vectors on a coordinate plane and discover the result of combining them.

•	Complete interactive exercises with parallel and perpendicular forces.
•	Draw vectors on a coordinate plane to show the magnitude and direction of the net force acting on an object.
•	Figure out how to resolve a vector into its x- and y-components.
•	Apply the Pythagorean theorem to resolve net forces.
•	See how tugboats pulling a ship can illustrate the combination of force vectors.

Name: AC Biology: Cells and Their Components
Description:
Extend your learning beyond a textbook. Explore science in a way that’s engaging and effective using interactive investigations and animations that let you control the way you learn.

Using 3-D models of an animal cell and a plant cell, compare and contrast the organelles within each cell. Then construct a Venn diagram to test your knowledge about which organelles are found in both plant and animal cells and which are unique to each type of cell.

•	Rotate and examine 3-D models of plant and animal cells.
•	Identify organelles that belong to either plant or animal cells, or both.
•	Describe the functions of various organelles.
•	Place organelles into an interactive Venn diagram.

Name: AC Biology: Classification of Bacteria
Description:
Take charge of your learning with interactive, exploratory exercises. Study the classification of bacteria on your device and change the way you learn science.

In a virtual laboratory, you’ll need to look closely at various bacterial samples to differentiate them based on their observable characteristics. After correctly identifying the samples, you’ll learn the importance of classifying bacteria.

•	Classify bacteria into groups based on their shape, cell walls, and growth requirements.
•	Identify bacteria by the amount of oxygen and type of nutrition they need.
•	Distinguish between four different common bacterial shapes.
•	Learn how to examine Gram-stained bacteria.
•	Record your observations as you perform tests in a laboratory.
•	Understand that the classification of bacteria allows the correct usage of antibiotics.

Name: AC Biology: Osmosis
Description:
It’s time to take learning to the next level. Get involved in your own learning with interactive explorations and animations.

Conduct a series of experiments to determine the best solute concentration for a new sports drink. In order to do this, you will explore hypertonic, hypotonic, and isotonic solutions.

•	Experiment with a virtual compound microscope.
•	Experience a lab environment where you are “doing,” not just watching.
•	Investigate the effect of hypertonic, hypotonic, and isotonic solutions.
•	Evaluate your hypothesis after completing the experiment.
•	Describe osmosis across a semipermeable membrane.

Name: AC Biology: Factors Influencing Photosynthesis: Intensity and the Color of Light
Description:
It’s a new way to learn and understand science. Get involved with highly interactive activities and take your learning to a different level.

Observe how the color of light and temperature affect oxygen production during photosynthesis. By experimenting with aquatic plants and varying the intensity and color of light, you can observe the oxygen released as a byproduct of these changes and determine their effects on photosynthesis.

•	Explain how plants get energy.
•	Describe how the intensity of light affects the rate of photosynthesis.
•	Explain the impact of different colors on the rate of photosynthesis.
•	Identify the optimum color and intensity of light in which photosynthesis occurs.
•	Evaluate graphs and tables to gather, analyze, and interpret data

Name: AC Biology: Mendel’s Experiment
Description:
Learn science by investigating challenging topics and performing experiments within a highly interactive setting. It’s all about taking control of the way you learn.

Investigate the results of cross-pollinating pea plants as you replicate Gregor Mendel’s experiments. Then learn how a pair of alleles can control the expression of traits. 

•	Cross-pollinate pea plants and observe the traits of the offspring.
•	Perform experimental crosses to create F1 and F2 generation pea plants.
•	Make predictions about the results of your experiments.
•	Recognize the difference between recessive and dominant traits.

Name: AC Life Science: The Nervous System
Description:
Become an active participant in your learning as you investigate the human body. Watch animations, complete interactive exercies, answer questions, and take quizzes—learn science in a new way.

Look inside the human body to explore the nervous system, a complex collection of nerves and specialized cells that transmit signals throughout the body. First, learn about the parts of the nervous system, including neuron cells and their components. Then test your knowledge by matching structures of the nervous system with their functions using an interactive model.

•	Discover the purpose, use, and importance of the nervous system.
•	Identify different structures that make up the central and peripheral nervous systems.
•	Learn about neurons and how they function.
•	Explore the three regions of the brain.
•	Match structures of the nervous system with their functions.

Name: AC Biology: Introduction to Protists
Description:
There’s a better way to learn and experience the world of science. Take part in interactive, highly visual activities that let you manipulate objects in a virtual environment to learn all about them.

Explore the Kingdom Protista as you perform various tests on six different types of protists, including algae, slime molds, and ciliates. By examining the protists under a microscope and completing a dichotomous key, you’ll be able to classify each protist according to its characteristics.

•	Study characteristics of the Kingdom Protista.
•	Perform lab tests and collect data on various protists.
•	Differentiate among protists based on nutrition and digestion styles, and whether they have structures that enable movement.
•	Identify the means of locomotion of specific protists.
•	Complete a dichotomous key.

Name: AC Biology: Sorting and Identifying Animal Fossils
Description:
There’s a better way to learn and experience the world of science. Take part in interactive, highly visual activities that let you manipulate objects in a virtual environment to learn all about them.

Examine various animal fossils and sort them based on their common characteristics. Then learn how a classification key can be used to identify the fossils of an animal’s teeth, jaws, scales, or vertebrae.

•	Identify the different characteristics of fossils from dinosaurs, bony fish, and other animals.
•	Find out how a classification key is useful in identifying fossils.
•	See why the study of fossil records indicates the evolution of organisms over time.  
•	Consider the evolution of birds from flightless dinosaurs to the modern birds of today.
•	Learn about the various types of fossils and the ways in which organisms can be fossilized.
•	Discover the type of rock in which fossils usually form.
•	Understand why scientists examine homologies, biogeography, and the fossil record to explore common ancestries among organisms.

Name: AC Biology: Effect of pH on Enzyme Activity
Description:
Get involved in learning with highly interactive and engaging science activities. It’s all about doing and becoming an active participant in your own learning. The time is now, so get started and see where it takes you.

Using the human digestive system as an example, learn how two enzymes—pepsin and peptidase—function best at a specific pH. To do so, you’ll have to test their enzymatic activity in the lab using egg whites and solutions of varying pH levels.

•	Discover how pH affects enzymatic activity.
•	Experiment with two digestive enzymes to determine the pH at which they work best.
•	Make hypotheses and analyze the results of your experiment.
•	Graph your observations of the effect of pH on enzyme activity.
•	Explore how the optimum pH for digestive enzymes relates to their location in the human body.

Name: AC Life Science: Comparing Plant and Animal Cells
Description:
Extend your learning beyond a textbook. Explore science in a way that’s engaging and effective using interactive investigations and animations that let you control the way you learn.

“Greencity” and “Citymalia” (two cities representing a plant and animal cell, respectively) need your help in assigning agents (organelles) to solve particular problems. By assigning agents to various tasks within the cities, you’ll learn the differences between plant and animal cell organelles and their functions.

•	Use an analogy to differentiate between the organelles of plant and animal cells.
•	Assign agents, which represent specific organelles, to address various problems.
•	Identify organelles that belong to either plant or animal cells, or both.
•	Describe the functions of various organelles.
•	Place organelles into an interactive Venn diagram.

Name: Life Science: Muscles and Pinocchio’s Arm
Description:
Get involved in exploring various parts of the human body with engaging, interactive science activities. It’s all about doing and actively participating in your own learning. The time is now, so get started and see where it takes you.

Explore the functions and purposes of muscles in the human body. Using materials such as pieces of wood, springs, string, or rubber bands, try your hand at constructing one of Pinocchio’s arms to discover how muscles work at a joint and how they also work in pairs.

•	Learn how muscles are the structures that produce movement in the skeletal system. 
•	Construct Pinocchio’s right arm using everyday materials.
•	Figure out which materials represent the bones of a real arm and the fluid between the skeletal joints.
•	Understand why muscles frequently work in pairs.
•	Watch an animation showing how muscles work in pairs.

Name: AC Life Science: Exploring Cells with a Microscope
Description:
Take learning into your own hands! Use virtual tools to explore cells under a microscope. It’s a new way to learn and understand science. 

Manipulate four parts of a compound light microscope to bring various human tissue samples into clear view. Learn how to adjust the lens, diaphragm, course focus knob, and fine focus knob to get just the right amount of magnification, focus, and light for each sample.

•	Operate and adjust a compound microscope to examine cells of human tissue.
•	Identify the parts of a compound microscope.
•	Find out how the lens, diaphragm, course focus knob, and fine focus knob function on a microscope.
•	Get feedback to help you choose the right parts to adjust for the clearest images possible.

Name: AC Biology: Discovering the Function of the Nucleus
Description:
The time has come to experience science like never before! Complete virtual experiments, make predictions, and draw conclusions. Bring science to your device and take control of your learning.

Conduct experiments similar to those performed by the scientist Joachim Hämmerling to discover the role that the nucleus plays in cells. Using a scalpel and a micro-injector in a virtual lab, cut a single-celled alga into different parts and then remove its nucleus.

•	Discover the unique features of the giant unicellular species of Acetabularia.
•	Repeat Hämmerling’s experiments on algae.
•	Predict whether an alga will survive if its base, stalk, or cap is removed.
•	Carry out experiments to test your hypotheses.
•	Find out the function of the nucleus in cells.

Name: AC Biology: Hardy-Weinberg Equation
Description:
What better way to learn those tough concepts in science than to carry out hands-on, highly visual activities that let you investigate challenging topics in a virtual environment. 

Delve into the details of evolution as you study the Hardy-Weinberg equation and learn how it can be used to provide evidence of natural selection acting upon a population. Various interactive exercises help you learn about the two forms of the equation and the conditions necessary for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

•	Discover that a recessive phenotype can be more common than a dominant phenotype.
•	Learn how to calculate p and q in a population.
•	Explore the change in allele frequencies that can happen over time.
•	Understand how such factors as gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, and natural selection can lead to evolution.
•	Discover how genetic equilibrium is expressed in a population.

Name: AC Life Science: Habitat Designer: Pandas
Description:
Learn science in a way that is engaging and effective. Complete interactive actvities and quizzes, access helpful feedback and key vocabulary―and do it all right there on your device!

Demonstrate your knowledge of ecosystems by designing a habitat for a population of endangered giant pandas. To be successful, you must consider the most appropriate elements that will help the pandas survive.

•	Examine the components of ecosystems and populations.
•	Access information about the habitat requirements of giant pandas.
•	Choose the appropriate size for the pandas’ habitat.
•	Learn about different types of ecosystems.
•	Select the best flora and fauna for the pandas’ habitat.
•	Choose the most suitable monitoring systems and fencing structures to protect the pandas.

Name: AC Biology: Factors Influencing Photosynthesis: Carbon Dioxide
Description:
Take charge of your learning! Explore photosynthesis in an engaging and interactive environment. 

Determine how and why carbon dioxide affects the rate of photosynthesis. Learn the chemical equation for photosynthesis, discuss how carbon dioxide affects the rate of photosynthesis, conduct an experiment, and analyze the results.

•	Participate in a scientific investigation on photosynthesis.
•	Identify the required substances for photosynthesis to occur.
•	Determine the products of photosynthesis.
•	Explain the effect of carbon dioxide on photosynthesis.
•	Draw a conclusion based on your investigation using data, graphs, and tables.

Name: AC Biology: Analysis of Fossil Evidence
Description:
Take charge of your learning! Explore paleontology in an engaging and interactive environment where you get to examine the evidence of past life. 

Play the role of a paleontologist as you learn to organize and analyze fossil evidence. Using fossils of fish, turtles, dinosaurs, and other animals, investigate two important steps involved in fossil analysis—organization and interpretation. Then draw your own conclusions about fish populations in prehistoric marine environments. 

•	Analyze fossil teeth, jaws, vertebrae, and scales from various past life forms.
•	Discover what kinds of questions can be answered by examining fossils. 
•	Find out which parts of organisms are most easily fossilized.
•	Identify a testable hypothesis from the fossil evidence of fish. 
•	Draw correct conclusions from fossil evidence.
•	Learn the steps used to analyze fossils.

Name: AC Biology: The Cell Cycle and Mitosis
Description:
Learn science by investigating challenging topics within a highly visual setting. With interactive science activities on your device, endless learning opportunities are right at your fingertips.

Examine human cheek cells under a microscope in order to learn about the phases of the cell cycle and the stages of mitosis. First, identify cells that are in the process of division; then match each cell with the phase of the cell cycle it is undergoing. 

•	Discover the events that occur in each phase of the cell cycle.
•	Examine cells under a microscope.
•	Match individual cells with phases of the cell cycle.
•	View animations that depict the cell cycle.

Name: AC Biology: Surface Area-to-Volume Ratio in Organisms
Description:
Learn science in a way that is engaging and effective. Take part in interactive simulations that let you manipulate objects in a virtual environment to learn all about them.

Change the length of the sides of an interactive 3-D cube to see how it affects its surface area and volume. Then after studying surface area-to-volume ratios, learn how this ratio influences the rate of heat loss in objects and in animals.

•	Manipulate the size of a cube to observe changes to its surface area and volume.
•	Collect data and analyze a graph.
•	Calculate surface area-to-volume ratios.
•	Compare the surface area-to-volume ratio of small and large organisms.
•	Consider examples of organisms’ adaptations to minimize heat loss.

Name: AC Life Science: Agent Organelles
Description:
Learn science in a way that’s engaging and effective. Explorations and animations in an interactive environment let you extend your learning beyond a textbook.

Using the analogy of a city run by various workers, called agents, you must tackle a number of problems by matching each task with the agent whose skills are best suited to solve the situation at hand. In the process, discover the functions of various organelles and inclusions in a cell.

•	Assign agents to fix problems that arise in a city.
•	Pair each agent with a task based on the agent’s unique skills.
•	Consider the roles that organelles play in a plant cell.
•	Learn about the functions of a cell’s nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and more.
•	Look at the structures of plant cells.

Name: AC Life Science: Environmental Factors That Affect the Growth of Molds
Description:
Take part in virtual lab experiments as you explore the world of biology. It’s about doing and experiencing science, not just reading about it.

Examine a piece of moldy bread to learn more about mold, its relationship to fungi, and how mold reproduces through spores. Then carry out an experiment to investigate the effects of light, temperature, and moisture on the growth of mold.

•	Learn about the characteristics of mold and fungi.
•	Discover how mold reproduces through spores.
•	Conduct an experiment to determine the right environmental conditions for mold growth.
•	Hypothesize about the effects of light, temperature, and moisture on mold growth.
•	Practice gathering, analyzing, and interpreting data.
•	Learn about organisms that belong to the Kingdom Fungi.

Name: AC Biology: Commensalism
Description:
Study the relationships that exist among different species in nature with interactive learning opportunities. Complete experiments, answer questions, make predictions, and take quizzes—learn science in a whole new way.

In a virtual aquatic environment, place a shark and a remora together in a tank and observe their interactions. Then learn more about commensalism and study examples of other types of symbiotic relationships, such as those between a crocodile and plover bird and between a dog and tick.

•	Find out whether or not remora fish are in danger by living alongside sharks.
•	Make predictions about how the shark and remora will interact, and then investigate your hypotheses.
•	Observe what happens when you combine the two species in the same aquarium in a virtual lab.
•	Analyze graphs of data showing changes in the two species’ body weight, and then make conclusions.
•	See if you can correctly match up organisms that have commensal relationships.

Name: AC Biology: Introduction to Classification
Description:
Why not experience and do science rather than just reading about it! With highly interactive activities, you see it, do it, practice it, and apply it. Study organisms and learn to classify them right on your device.

In Introduction to Classification, it’s your job to examine the features of insects and use them to create a dichotomous key and a classification system. In doing so, discover why classification systems are so important to biologists.

•	Use a library as an analogy to help understand the importance of classification.
•	Learn the practical applications of classification systems.
•	Identify unknown organisms based on their physical characteristics.
•	Create a dichotomous key for use as an identification tool.
•	Build a simple classification system and apply it.

Name: AC Biology: Structure and Function of the Cell Membrane
Description:
Open up a whole new way of learning with AC apps! Get ready to experience engaging and interactive learning opportunities.

In Structure and Function of the Cell Membrane, explore the various structures and functions of the cell membrane by using a cell model. Learn about cell transport methods and how they are grouped into two categories: those that require energy expenditure by a cell and those that do not.

•	Discover the commonalities of a security guard and cells.
•	Explore the different transport methods of cells.
•	Examine how the structure of a cell relates to its function.
•	Experience cells and how they work.
•	Practice gathering, analyzing, and interpreting data.
•	Identify the parts of a cell.

Name: VClass Teacher
Description:
Sebit VClass Teacher app lets teacher create a classroom session, and work with lesson plans, study plans and tests & quizzes.

This application requires a valid Sebit VCloud account.

Name: AC Biology: DNA to Protein Synthesis
Description:
Get involved in learning with highly interactive and engaging science activities. It’s all about doing and becoming an active participant in your own learning. The time is now, so get started and see where it takes you.

To help a team of scientists that have fallen ill, you must find an antibiotic that’s effective against the disease-causing bacterium. To do so, you’ll need to study the process of protein synthesis and learn how antibiotics prevent protein production in bacteria.

•	Manipulate an interactive DNA model.
•	Explore the process of protein synthesis.
•	Identify the part of the cell where amino acids are assembled into proteins.
•	Pair the bases in nucleic acids.
•	Learn how to use a codon table.
•	Review the details of transcription and translation.

Name: VClass
Description:
Student version of Sebit VClass app displays the list of the classroom activities performed within a session.

This application requires a valid Sebit VCloud account.

Name: AC Biology: Cell Theory and Cell Types
Description:
There’s a better way to learn and experience the world of science. Take part in interactive, highly visual activities that let you manipulate objects in a virtual environment to learn all about them.

In order to understand the cell theory, review the contributions key scientists made to its development throughout history and identify its three basic tenets. Then stain and observe cell samples under a microscope to identify them as prokaryotic or eukaryotic. 

•	Discover historical milestones made by Robert Hooke and other scientists.
•	Identify the three basic tenets of cell theory.
•	Stain cell samples with different dyes to observe their organelles.
•	Classify cell samples as prokaryotic or eukaryotic.
•	Review the differences between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.

Name: AC Life Science: Joints
Description:
There’s a whole new way to learn science. Jump in and start exploring the human body, starting with the skeletal system. The time is now, so get started and find out where it takes you.

See whether you can identify the joints that move as someone throws a basketball. Then learn about the different kinds of movable joints in the human body, from head to toe. 

•	Detect six joints that move while shooting a basketball.
•	Recognize joints as the place in the skeletal system where two or more bones come together.
•	Identify four types of movable joints.
•	Distinguish between pivot, ball-and-socket, hinge, and gliding joints.

Name: AC Life Science: Aerobic Respiration in Plants
Description:
The time has come to experience science like never before! With engaging and highly interactive activities, you get to see it, do it, practice it, and apply it. Bring science to your device and take control of your learning.

To learn more about how photosynthesis and aerobic respiration occur in plants, conduct some experiments and analyze the results. By measuring the carbon dioxide produced by a plant, you’ll discover when plants perform aerobic respiration.

•	Explore the process of aerobic respiration in plants.
•	Conduct an experiment to determine when aerobic respiration occurs.
•	Make a hypothesis and then test it.
•	Monitor the amount of carbon dioxide a plant produces day and night.
•	Practice gathering, analyzing, and interpreting data.

Name: AC Biology: Biological Adaptations - Bird Beaks
Description:
Venture into a whole new way of learning with AC Biology apps! Get ready to experience learning opportunities full of interactive tasks, investigations, and animations.

To apply for a job at a zoo where you’ll be responsible for feeding four types of birds, you must prove that you can correctly identify the type of food each bird eats based on the shape of its beak. Then learn how the shapes of birds’ beaks are just one example of biological adaptations that help organisms survive in their respective environments.

•	Train for a job feeding different bird species at a zoo.
•	Match differently shaped beaks of birds with the specific types of food each bird eats. 
•	See how adaptations help organisms eat and survive in their environments.
•	Given different situations, choose the adaptation that would most likely help animals survive.

Name: Love Quotes!
Description: A crazy lover? You will like this app reading the best quotes everyday to you beloved lover, wife, soul mate, to anyone you want to fall in love, use it!

Name: AC Life Science: The Life Cycle of Animals
Description:
Don’t just read about science—interact with it in a dynamic, interactive environment! Carry out your own investigations and activities to learn all about biology.

Discover the life cycles of different organisms, including a chicken, a butterfly, a cockroach, and a frog. Create colorful posters by placing photos of animals into the correct spots to represent the different stages of their life cycles.

•	Learn the different stages of the life cycles of insects, birds, amphibians, and mammals.
•	Take photos of animals in various stages of their life cycles.
•	Collect information about different organisms and investigate their developmental stages.
•	Create a poster that shows the life cycle of each animal.
•	Learn about metamorphosis in different types of insects.
•	Compare and contrast the stages of development in different animals.

Name: Physics: Electric Current & Resistance
Description:
Unique … Personalized … Interactive … Engaging

It’s a New Way of Learning and It Starts NOW

Get ready to enter the AC Vbook library and start your technology-based learning adventure with Electric Current and Resistance. Experience the world of standards-based textbook content with highly interactive explorations, visual explanations and exercises—all focused on understanding a physics concept.

Physics has never been so real!

The time to immerse yourself in a new way of learning is now. Let’s get started!

Get engaged in the world of Physics: … the what … the how … and the why.

Have you ever wondered what happens when you turn on your desk lamp?

Ever wonder what else Ben Franklin was known for?

Investigate how electric current is formed.

Examine the relationship between electric current and potential difference.

Explore resistance to determine what factors affect it.

Learn how to calculate electric current and apply Ohm’s law.

Name: Physics: Series and Parallel Circuits
Description:
AC VBooks Provide a Whole New Way of Learning… Starting Now!

Jump into the world of standards-based content with highly interactive explorations, visual explanations, and exercises—all focused on understanding a physics concept. AC VBooks offer exciting, personalized activities with widgets and cool graphics that can’t be found in textbooks. Enter the AC VBook library and begin exploring with the “Series and Parallel Circuits” app. It’s physics like you’ve never seen before!  

Learn about it… See it in action… Practice it…

Check your understanding of key concepts—all on your Win8 tablet or computer.

Investigate the differences between series, parallel, and complex circuits.

Explore Ohm’s law.

Calculate the amount of current moving through a circuit.

Examine the behavior of current traveling through different circuits.

Understand why light bulbs may or may not go out when another light bulb goes out in a circuit.

Represent resistance in pictures, equations, and statements.

Investigate equivalent resistance.


The AC VBook titled “Physics – Series and Parallel Circuits” walks you through the following topics:

Series Circuits

Name: Algebra 1: Linearity, Slope, & Direct Variation
Description:
Unique… Personalized… Interactive… Engaging

It’s a New Way of Learning and It Starts NOW

Enter the AC VBook library and begin your experience with Linearity, Slope, and Direct Variation. Jump into the world of standards-based textbook content with highly interactive explorations, visual explanations and exercises—all focused on understanding important Algebra concepts.

It’s Algebra like you’ve never seen before. 

Learn about it. See it in action. Practice it. Check your understanding. And do it all on your tablet or computer.

Explore the difference between an independent and a dependent variable.

Calculate the average rate of change.

Examine variables and graph a linear function.

Explore and identify the different types of slope.

Understand the difference between constant and varying quantities.

Discover how the constant of variation and slope are connected.

Represent direct variations in tables, equations and statements. 



This AC VBook Algebra walks you through the following topics:

The Concept of Linearity
    Dependent and Independent Variables
    Average Rate of Change
         Calculating Average Rate of Change
    Linear Relationships
         Constant Average Rate of Change
         Graphs of Linear Relationships

The Concept of Slope
    Average Rate of Change

Direct Variation

Name: Geometry: Circumference & Arc Length
Description:
Unique … Personalized … Interactive … Engaging

It’s a New Way of Learning and It Starts NOW

Get ready to enter the AC Vbook library and start your technology-based learning adventure with Circumference and Arc Length. Experience the world of standards-based textbook content with highly interactive explorations, visual explanations and exercises—all focused on understanding a mathematical concept.  

Geometry has never been easier!

It’s time.  Take your learning to a new level and get involved from the start.

Have you ever wondered how the number pi was discovered?  

Curious about how circumference, diameter and radius are connected?  

Interested in learning the relationships between arc length, circumference and angle measurement? 

Discover how radius and arc length impact concentric circles?  

Check your readiness, explore Circumference and Arc, and test your understanding.

Download the AC Vbook Geometry: Circumference and Arc Length App and find answers to those questions and more.


AC Vbook Geometry: Circumference and Arc Length App takes you through the following topics:

Circumference of a Circle tackles:
	The Circle and Its Elements
	How Do You Find the Circumference of a Circle?
	The Relationship Between The Circumference and Diameter of a Circle
	The Formula of the Circumference of a Circle

Arc Length of a Circle includes experience with:
	Arcs and Ways to Measure Their Size 
	The Relationship Between Arc Length, Circumference, and Arc Length
	Finding the Arc Length Given the Measure of the Central Angle
	What is the Relationship Between Radius and Arc Length?
	Proportional Relationship between Radius and Arc Length

Name: AC Physics: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
Description:
Be actively engaged in how you learn some of the basic laws that govern science every day. Complete experiments, answer questions, make predictions, and take quizzes—learn science in a new way.

Conduct experiments with balanced and unbalanced forces to see whether an object remains stationary or moves in a certain direction. Find out the simple math involved in calculating the net force on an object and predicting the result that the force will have on the object’s motion.

•	Watch how a tug-of-war game demonstrates balanced and unbalanced forces.
•	Discover what happens when two equal forces or two unequal forces are applied to an object at rest.
•	Find out how to calculate the net force of balanced and unbalanced forces.
•	Predict the direction in which an object will move after calculating its net force.
•	See why objects under the influence of unbalanced forces accelerate.

Name: AC Biology: Hidden Heroes: Bacteria
Description:
Take control of what and how you learn with engaging and highly interactive activities. It’s all about doing―experiencing science, not just reading about it.

Head down into an underground biology laboratory where you’ll carry out a secret mission to produce a specialized bacterium that might help solve environmental problems. As you engineer a new strain resistant to heat and radiation, you’ll learn more about bioremediation.

•	Navigate a virtual laboratory.
•	Choose scientists with the right skills to help with the mission.
•	Consult bacteria, bioremediation, and waste management textbooks.
•	Study the characteristics of six particular bacteria species.
•	Perform heat and radiation tests on bacterial cells.

Description: Fotógrafo amateur? Fotógrafo apasionado? Te encanta la fotografía a fin de cuentas no? Descarga está aplicación para saber un poco más sobre aquello que en verdad amas.

Name: AC Life Science: The Nucleus and Control of a Cell: Hämmerling’s Experiment with Algae
Description:
The time has come to experience science like never before! Complete virtual experiments, make predictions, and draw conclusions. Bring science to your device and take control of your learning.

Conduct experiments similar to those performed by the scientist Joachim Hämmerling to discover the role that the nucleus plays in cells. Using a scalpel and a micro-injector in a virtual lab, cut a single-celled alga into different parts and then remove its nucleus.

•	Discover the unique features of the giant unicellular species of Acetabularia.
•	Repeat Hämmerling’s experiments on algae.
•	Predict whether an alga will survive if its base, stalk, or cap is removed.
•	Carry out experiments to test your hypotheses.
•	Find out the function of the nucleus in cells.

Name: AC Biology: Pangaea: Image of Earth 250 Million Years Ago
Description:
Get involved in learning with highly interactive and engaging science activities. It’s all about doing and becoming an active participant in your own learning. The time is now, so get started and see where it takes you.

Investigate the hypothesis that the continents were once joined together in a supercontinent called Pangaea. Explore evidence, form the supercontinent Pangaea using the continents as they are shaped today, and study mantle convection, seafloor spreading, and plate tectonics.

•	Explain the fossil, climate, and geological evidence that supports that Pangaea existed.
•	Use models to support and interpret observations.
•	Understand Wegener’s hypothesis of continental drift.
•	Describe plate tectonics.
•	Develop descriptions, explanations, predictions, and models using evidence.

Name: AC Biology: Identifying Cancerous Cells
Description:
Take a closer look at a very important topic of study in biology today: cancer. Examine healthy and cancerous cells through an interactive exercise that puts you in control of your own learning.

Assume the role of a doctor who must distinguish between healthy cells in one of the different stages of cell division versus abnormal cells that may indicate cancer. After identifying the cancerous cells, learn about common causes of cancer as well as the symptoms of lung cancer.

•	Recognize abnormal cells in the cell cycle.
•	Learn how cancer cells are produced by mutations that cause rapid, uncontrolled cell growth.
•	Study the formation, structure, and organization of cells.
•	Discover the symptoms of lung cancer.
•	Identify the three leading causes of cancer.

Name: AC Biology: Chemosynthesis
Description:
Go beyond the standard textbooks and take learning to the next level. Complete virtual experiments, consider exploratory scenarios, make predictions and conclusions—learn science in a new way.

Dive deep down into a virtual ocean to explore the relationship between bacteria and tubeworms living near hydrothermal vents. Investigate how the bacteria and tubeworms are able to survive without relying on energy from the sun.

•	Look at underwater ecosystems near volcanically active areas where complex communities rely on chemical energy rather than sunlight for their survival.
•	Learn how some organisms can synthesize organic compounds from inorganic compounds. 
•	Observe how chemosynthesis is carried out by certain species of bacteria. 
•	Carry out laboratory experiments to test for chemosynthetic reactions.
•	Understand the symbiotic relationship between tubeworms and bacteria that exist near hydrothermal vents.

Name: AC Biology: Diffusion
Description:
Take charge of your learning! Explore diffusion in a highly interactive environment. 

To learn about the process of diffusion, carry out a few experiments in which you’ll place dialysis tubing filled with a solution into a beaker containing another solution. Then observe how molecules pass through the selectively permeable membrane.

•	Learn about the selective permeability of cell membranes.
•	Experiment with the motion of molecules by diffusion.
•	Explore the effect of size on the diffusion of molecules through membranes.
•	Learn the difference between passive and facilitated diffusion.
•	Identify examples where diffusion has occurred.

Name: AC Life Science
Description:
Science: It’s the study of the physical and natural world all around us. So shouldn’t learning about life on Earth be active, exploratory, and as engaging as the subject itself? Move beyond the static text and images of textbooks and let the world of science come alive. Work in virtual laboratories to investigate photosynthesis or study people’s genetic characteristics, perform tests to understand how mold grows or create suitable habitats for pandas and sea turtles. 

From genetics to ecology, evolution to biological molecules, and more, the AC Life Science app provides a collection of interactive and animated content that lets you explore a variety of scientific concepts within virtual environments. For ease of use, all of the animations and activities available within the AC Life Science app are organized into units and study plans. So whether you choose to investigate Human Effects on Nature within the Ecology unit or to study Food and Digestion from the unit on Structure and Function in Living Systems, you’ll have a library of highly visual activities right there on your tablet. 

•	Access well organized units and study plans that group content by topic, including:
        o	Biological Molecules and Cells 
                	Levels of Organization 
                	Cell Structure
                	Cellular Energy
                	Cellular Transport
        o	Structure and Function in Living Systems 
                	Cell Division
                	Reproductive Systems
                	Movement and Support
                	Circulation
                	Respiration
                	Food and Digestion
                	Excretion
                	Human Body
                	Nervous System
                	Endocrine System
                	Sensory Organs
        o	Genetics and Heredity
                	Mendelian Genetics
                	Molecular Genetics
        o	Evolution, Diversity, and Classification
                	History of the Earth and Life
                	Evolution and Adaptation
                	Biodiversity
                	Classification
        o	Ecology
                	Organisms and Their Environment 
                	Interactions Among Organisms 
                	Population Dynamics
                	Energy Flow
                	Cycling of Matter
                	Human Effects on Nature
•	Carry out experiments, investigate concepts, make predictions, and answer questions.
•	Watch animations that illustrate challenging concepts with colorful graphics.
•	Use Venn diagrams, graphs, dichotomous keys, and more.

Name: AC Biology: Homeostasis
Description:
Go beyond the standard textbooks and take learning to the next level. Complete virtual experiments, consider exploratory scenarios, make predictions and conclusions—learn science in a whole new way.

Explore vacuoles in paramecia in order to learn about homeostasis. In a virtual lab, experiment with the effects of salt on the activity of a paramecium. Then study how organisms, including humans, use homeostasis to regulate their bodies.

•	Make a hypothesis and then conduct an investigation of paramecia.
•	Place a paramecium in solutions with different salt concentrations and study the activity of its vacuoles.
•	Identify examples of homeostasis in the human body.

Name: AC Life Science: Muscles and Pinocchio’s Arm
Description:
Get involved in exploring various parts of the human body with engaging, interactive science activities. It’s all about doing and actively participating in your own learning. The time is now, so get started and see where it takes you.

Explore the functions and purposes of muscles in the human body. Using materials such as pieces of wood, springs, string, or rubber bands, try your hand at constructing one of Pinocchio’s arms to discover how muscles work at a joint and how they also work in pairs.

•	Learn how muscles are the structures that produce movement in the skeletal system. 
•	Construct Pinocchio’s right arm using everyday materials.
•	Figure out which materials represent the bones of a real arm and the fluid between the skeletal joints.
•	Understand why muscles frequently work in pairs.
•	Watch an animation showing how muscles work in pairs.

Name: Algebra 1: Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs
Description:
The time has finally arrived!! Enter a whole new world of learning and become a 21st century learner with AC VBooks! 

Start learning today with standards-based textbook content presented with highly interactive explorations, visual explanations, animations, and hands-on exercises. 

AC VBooks are here and ready to engage you in your own learning. Get ready to experience exciting, instructionally focused math activities with hands-on interactivity that includes cool graphics and fun widgets. 

Enter the library of AC VBook apps and begin your learning adventure. Dive into algebra with the “Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs” VBook apps. 

Don’t just sit there—get started!

•	Take control of your learning. See it… Do it… Practice it... Apply it.
•	Learn the language of algebra: quadratic functions, parabolas, x-intercepts, and more.
•	Understand how quadratic functions and their parabolas apply to real-world scenarios.
•	Experience hands-on interactions, not just words and pictures on a page.
•	Identify differences between linear and quadratic functions. See them come to life right on your screen.
•	Determine what you have learned with formative and summative assessments.

The AC VBook titled “Algebra 1 — Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs” provides an introduction to quadratic functions, their components, and how to graph them by exploring the following sections:


Introducing the Quadratic Function 
	Do Heavier Objects Tall Taster than Lighter Ones?
	Definition of a Quadratic Function
	How to Identify a Quadratic Equation
	A Little Recap Lesson:  Linear Functions
	Identify the Quadratic Function Given in Different Representations
	Identify the Differences between a Linear and a Quadratic Function

Parabolas and Their Properties 
	Parabolas of Quadratic Functions
	Graphing Quadratic Functions by Using a Table of Values
	x and y-Intercepts of a Parabola
	Zeros of a Function and their Relationship to x-intercepts of the Related Parabolas
	The Axis of Symmetry of a Parabola
	The Vertex of a Parabola
	Minimum and Maximum Values of a Parabola
	Domain and Range of a Quadratic Function

Graphing Parabolas Using the Parent Function 
	Quadratic Parent Functions
	The Value of a in y = ax2  on the Graph of a Parabola
	Observing How the Parabola Changes for a>0
	The Value of c in y = ax2 + c on the Graph of a Parabola
	Compare the Graph of y = ax2 + c to the Graph of y=ax2

Graphing a Quadratic Function Given in General Form
	Key Characteristics of a Parabola
	Find the Axis of Symmetry for a Quadratic Function Given in General Form
	Find the Vertex for a Quadratic Function Given in General Form
	Find the y-intercept for a Quadratic Function Given in General Form
	Find Additional Points  for a Quadratic Function Given in General Form
	Graph a Quadratic Equation Given in General Form

Name: Test 20 Greek
Description: The Greek alphabet is the script that has been used to write the Greek language since the 8th century BC. It was derived from the earlier Phoenician alphabet, and was in turn the ancestor of numerous other European and Middle Eastern scripts, including Cyrillic and Latin. In its classical and modern form, the alphabet has 24 letters, ordered from alpha to omega. Like Latin and Cyrillic, Greek originally had only a single form of each letter; it developed the letter case distinction between upper-case and lower-case forms in parallel with Latin during the modern era. This quiz will help you to learning the Greek alphabet.

Name: Test 20 Katakana
Description: Katakana  is a Japanese syllabary, one component of the Japanese writing system along with hiragana, kanji, and in some cases the Latin script. The word katakana means "fragmentary kana", as the katakana characters are derived from components of more complex kanji.  used for transcription of foreign language words into Japanese and the writing of loan words. It is also used for emphasis, to represent onomatopoeia, and to write certain Japanese language words, such as technical and scientific terms, and the names of plants, animals, and minerals. Names of Japanese companies are also often written in katakana rather than the other systems. This quiz will help you learning this japanese syllabary.

Name: Test 20 Katakana with Hiragana
Description: Kana are syllabic Japanese scripts, a part of the Japanese writing system contrasted with the logographic Chinese characters known in Japan as kanji. There are three kana scripts: modern cursive hiragana, modern angular katakana. This quiz will help you to associating the hiragana with katakana.

Name: Test 20 Hiragana
Description: Hiragana is a Japanese syllabary, one basic component of the Japanese writing system, along with katakana, kanji, and in some cases the Latin-script alphabet.  Used to write native words for which there are no kanji, including grammatical particles and suffixes , hiragana is used to write words whose kanji form is obscure, not known to the writer or readers, or too formal for the writing purpose. This quiz will help you to learning this syllabary.

Name: Japanese Verb Group Quiz

The Group 1 formed by verbs end with "~ u", the group 2 formed by verbs end with either "~iru" or "~ eru" and group 3 formed by irregular verbs. This app will help you learning the japanese verb groups.

Name: Time in Japanese
